need: Place a gate between two posts or fence ends as a readable opening: an open leaf or panel with a visible frame, hinge posts that match the fence, and no lantern or stray block that reads as a pillar.
evidence: Rejected 'Make the garden gate read as a gate': a bare light block with a floating lantern beside the post reads as a stray unfinished pillar, and the open gate, fence and ivy were removed.

need: Chimney stacks should project a set height above the roof surface and take a dark cap material by default, with a check that the cap is not sunk into the roof covering or lit as a bright patch.
evidence: Rejected 'Chimney on the west gable': a single bright pale cap sunk into the dark slate reads as a light patch or hole, not a stack, and is barely visible at a glance.

tool: glance render (small roof and wall features)
need: The glance render should show small roof and wall features (chimney caps, signs, fixtures) at the distance the judge sees the whole building, so a feature that disappears at glance scale is flagged.
evidence: Rejected chimney: judged 'barely visible at a glance'. Rejected curtains: 'the street view looks the same as before'.

need: Before placing a sign, board or banner, check clearance from adjacent signs and fixtures on the same wall and refuse or warn when two signs would touch and merge into one banner.
evidence: Rejected 'Hang a second small sign by the barrel': the dark board butts directly against the READING ROOM sign so the two merge into one long banner, and the dark oak clashes with the lighter board.

need: Window dressing should be recessed inside the opening with a depth offset, and a clash check should block placement over hanging lanterns, signs or other wall-mounted props.
evidence: Rejected 'Curtains on the side and back windows': a flat, translucent red strip overlaps the hanging lantern and the wall beside the window, so the back window reads as cluttered.

need: Flag any block whose luminance or saturation is far outside the build's aged palette, and suggest a weathered block of the same role before placement. A pure white block on a mossy build should not pass.
evidence: Rejected 'Operator touch: clean quartz doorstep': a pure white quartz step is a stark bright patch against mossy grey stone, reading as a mismatched, unweathered tile.

need: An opening option for door and window reveal depth, so the frame sits recessed by a set number of blocks and casts a visible shadow edge, rather than being recoloured on the wall face.
evidence: Rejected 'Fix walkability readout and door reveal': the door-side panel was recoloured to dull grey and brown, which removed colour but did not visibly improve the door reveal at a glance.

need: Sign placement should take a legibility/size option, such as a minimum letter height or a fixed text-to-width ratio, and reject or warn when the sign text is smaller than a readable size at the target scale.
evidence: Rejected 'Make the sign legible and prominent': sign text unreadably tiny; the fix didn't make it more legible or prominent.

tool: fascia / sign band placement with opening clearance
need: A band or fascia brush that places a sign or beam only in solid wall zones above the openings and reports any overlap with window or door cells before it is applied.
evidence: Rejected sign task: new oak beam across the upper storey is a wide plain slab that covers the windows, so the window row looks blocked.

tool: gable apex cap / stepped peak (attached to the roof)
need: A brush that builds a stepped cap on a gable apex, with each course bonded to the roof and wall cells beneath it, so no block is left floating or detached.
evidence: Rejected 'Stepped stone peak above the gable': a boxy, detached stone lump floats above the gable with a visible hole beside it.

tool: palette by role (post / corner material for dark stone walls)
need: Corner and post material defaults should be chosen by contrast with the wall material role, and the palette check should flag wood posts or logs set against dark stone walls.
evidence: Rejected stepped-peak task: stripped log corner posts clash with the dark stone walls, so the roofline looks less crafted.

need: The renderer should offer an interior or through-window view, so that interior changes such as shelving and meeting rooms can be judged when they are not visible from outside.
evidence: Rejected 'Interior stock and meeting room': the changes are barely visible from outside, so the judge cannot see the work.

tool: lean-to / addition brush with wall-and-roof attachment
need: A lean-to or addition brush that bonds its roof to the host wall and sets its wall cells against the existing envelope, with an orphan-block check that flags any block with no solid face contact.
evidence: Rejected 'Plank/wool lean-to': a patchy strip of wool and plank bands, and a stray red cube sticks out from the side.

need: A check that lists every block with no face-adjacent support or structural connection to the build, so stray or floating cubes are caught before render review.
evidence: Stray red cube on the lean-to and detached stone above the gable; both were visible only in the render.

tool: palette by role (wool and other non-facade blocks on facades)
need: Palette-by-role guidance or a validator should reject wool and other non-architectural blocks as facade or roof material unless the role is marked as decorative.
evidence: Rejected lean-to: red and yellow wool blocks read as clutter on a building facade.

tool: glance-scale check (new, in the render/check step)
need: Report every detail whose on-screen footprint at the glance distance is below a threshold (e.g. a 1-block accent, a sign's small text, sparse patches), so builders see which details will vanish before judging.
evidence: Five rejections say the same thing: the plaque text, the lanterns, the quartz kick-plate, the weathered base and the roof texture are all too small or too sparse to read at a glance.

need: A plaque preset with a legible text scale and a gold-trim or gold-leaf frame option, so a name plate reads as gold lettering from the glance distance.
evidence: 'Make the name plaque legible and gold' was rejected: the text was unreadable and the plaque was not visibly gold.

tool: emblem / pictogram inlay on a gable or tympanum field (B.emblem, new)
need: Place a recognisable symbol (e.g. a scales or seal motif) as a contiguous, readable inlay inside a named wall field such as a pediment, using a small pattern library and a palette contrast rule.
evidence: 'Make the pediment seal read' was rejected: the bright quartz panels read as stray white patches, not as a seal.

need: A surface pattern option for roof coverings (staggered or mixed-block courses, tile-course rhythm, or a per-course tone alternation) with a contrast setting, so slopes read as crafted rather than as a flat single-material field.
evidence: 'Texture the roof slopes' was rejected: the slopes still read as flat grey stone-brick courses, and the added texture was barely perceptible.

need: Weathering presets with a minimum coverage and contrast floor for a band (e.g. a base course), so moss and cobble patches are visible at the glance distance rather than sprinkled sparsely.
evidence: 'Weathered base on the flanks and rear' was rejected: a few mossy and cobble patches were barely visible in either view.

tool: lantern / light fixture anchored to architectural features (B.lantern, new, or a placement option on pilaster caps and posts)
need: Attach lanterns to a named feature top (pilaster cap, post top, wall top) by role instead of by coordinates, at a size that reads at the glance distance, and check that the light source does not add a stray colour cast.
evidence: 'Lamps on the side pilaster caps' was rejected: the lanterns were tiny specks, did not sit on the caps, and the build had no pilaster-cap placement rule.

need: A sill or kick-plate treatment that spans the full width of the opening as a continuous band, not one or two cells, with a default that defeats the stray-block look.
evidence: 'Clean quartz kick-plate under the east gallery windows' was rejected: the strip was a tiny accent that read as a stray bright block, not as a kick-plate.

tool: mcd render (per-job before/after diff + close-up crop)
need: For each detail job, render a before/after pair with a changed-cell count and a zoomed crop of the changed region, so sub-block edits are visible to the judge. A job that changes 0 cells must report 0, not look like a successful no-op.
evidence: About 25 'no visible change' observations across jobs (e.g. 'A and B pixel-identical in all four views', 'changes too subtle to read'). Full-size views cannot show 1-block texture.

need: Default variants must change colour value or relief by a visible step (a contrasting block family or a 1-block recess), and any variant below a minimum contrast should be rejected. Same-family near-tone swaps read as no-ops.
evidence: Wall field variation (deepslate, west flank, front) invisible; roof tile variation identical; shaft flank banding and elevator-head banding invisible; chimney texture invisible; deepslate lintels same colour as surround; pier grain only subtle.

need: A band option that projects the course one block proud and runs continuously between storeys on every face, so storey lines read in the silhouette.
evidence: Mid string course between storeys not visible in either render; shaft flank storey bands add no visible profile.

need: A projecting hood (slab or stair cap) over each opening head, with a proud-depth parameter, so window heads cast a visible shadow line.
evidence: Drip hoods over every window produced pixel-identical renders, or were too small to see.

need: Capital and end-cap options for piers and sign bands, so pillar tops and band ends are distinct from the shaft.
evidence: Entrance sign band end-caps and pillar capitals show no visible change in either build.

need: Default lantern placement should mount on a visible post or bracket at door height, sized to resolve at full view. Lanterns placed at default positions are lost at render scale.
evidence: Portico base lanterns not visible in either render; the job added no discernible detail.

need: Coping must be one continuous course on the wall-top ring. Stray placement off the ring is a defect, and the job should fail if the ring is not closed.
evidence: Roof-edge coping left stray specks on the rooftop with no edge improvement; roof-line coping on the front frieze not visible.

need: Options for a base flare or plinth ring and a shoulder corbel ring on towers and drums, so the base and shoulder read in the silhouette.
evidence: Tower base and shoulder: the only change was faint block texture on the shaft; the base and shoulder did not improve.

need: A weathering variant (mossy or cracked stone, darker step) reachable from detailing, not only from landscaping moss, so the base reads as weathered.
evidence: Mossy weathered base and plinth weathering/moss invisible; the stepped plinth in one build was the only visible change.

need: Opening and lintel jobs should enumerate openings from the element map per face. A job with zero targets must report a blocker, not write nothing and pass silently.
evidence: Window lintels (front and west flank) and the back door frame showed no change; the back door is not visible in either render, so the job likely had no target.

need: Report cells written per rule and warn or fail when a rule writes zero cells, so a no-op detail job is caught before review instead of being judged as a finished change.
evidence: Detail jobs 'Eaves cornice, west wall top', 'Stair-shaft glazing grid', 'Roof edge trim, north gable and shaft head' and 'Roof edge' each changed no visible pixels in any view.

tool: roof edge trim / coping / eaves cornice
need: Give roof-edge treatments a default projection and course depth that reads at full-build scale, so a coping or trim change is visible without hand-tuning sizes.
evidence: 'Roof edge' (JOB 11) had only a tiny vent and cap change; 'Roof edge coping' (JOB 10) showed no meaningful roof-edge profile at street view.

tool: weathering / speckle treatment (mcd paint vary, mossy and cracked variants)
need: Weather by contiguous course or panel with a coverage fraction and clustering, instead of scattering single cracked or mossy blocks that read as random noise.
evidence: Plinth mossy and cracked variation, wall-field cracked-deepslate patches, shaft-wall and elevator-head stone swaps, oak chute plank patches and wall texture were all judged faint, random speckle.

need: Default to a projection depth that casts a visible profile line over the full opening width, so sills and lintels read as profiles rather than sparse stubs or nothing.
evidence: 'Upper window lintels (front)' showed no visible lintel profile; 'Upper window sills (side)' added only tiny sparse plank stubs.

need: Accept an avoid or protected-cell set (as landscaping's avoidCells does) so sill, lintel and trim passes never cut into pilasters, piers or other reserved cells.
evidence: 'Window sills and lintels (north)' added ragged dark blocks that cut into the timber pilasters and cluttered the elevation, making it worse.

need: Provide a pilaster capital and base brush built from stair and slab courses in a specified material, so capitals and bases read as crafted profiles without stray diagonal bands. Cause not yet verified; the observation alone does not show whether the bands came from orientation, material or geometry.
evidence: 'Pilaster capitals and bases (north)' added large flat grey diagonal bands across the white portico and pilasters, which read as artifacts and broke the clean portico.

need: Render a per-job close-up and changed-pixel count at detail scale alongside the glance render, so the judge can see small detail changes instead of marking them neutral.
evidence: Most neutral verdicts (plinth, wall field, lintels, sills, chute, wall texture) said the change was too faint to see at full-build scale, so the judge could not assess it.

need: Hang a banner as one clean full-height panel on a pilaster or column face with a fixed width, no broken slivers, and an optional lantern hung below it.
evidence: JOB 7 teal banners read as a striped patch with a stray lantern off the column edge; JOB 2 banners became fragmented slivers with floating white bits

need: Lay out a short word or phrase as legible block-letter strokes across a sign band at a given height and width, with a fallback that reads as a plaque when the letters cannot fit.
evidence: JOB 1 gold lettering read as scattered gold blocks and orange teeth, not legible DEEPSLATE HOLDINGS text

need: Default pilasters and quoins to proud depth 2 with a contrasting role material, since depth 1 in the wall material is invisible at glance scale.
evidence: JOB 2 pilasters proud of the wall and dark quoins: before and after renders nearly identical; JOB 8 pier capitals and base blocks not visible

need: Show sub-block relief at a readable scale (close oblique view plus a before/after diff highlight) so the judge can see small finish changes.
evidence: JOB 4, JOB 8, JOB 21, JOB 26, JOB 35: before and after crops look identical, so real relief changes are unverifiable

tool: visibility / exposure check (proposed: mcd check visible)
need: Flag any detail placement that has no exposed face in the standard views, before the build is accepted.
evidence: JOB 16 flagpole rod changed no visible pixels in any view

tool: railing round any flat top (detail-language JOB 4 railing)
need: Run a single-height railing round the perimeter of any flat roof or tower top, with regular posts, a continuous top rail, and no pickets poking above merlons or parapets.
evidence: JOB 15 tower-top railing: stray pickets, uneven cross-bars, cluttered spiky tangle instead of a clean rail

need: Offer a slender gold or accent-role spire finial for gable peaks and roof ends, with the material drawn from the palette role rather than a bright default.
evidence: JOB 12 finial is an orange-red ball on a thin stalk, clashing with the slate and gold palette; concept has slender gold spires

need: Build a continuous stair-stepped raking band that follows the roof pitch with no gaps, at a set thickness and material, along both gable edges.
evidence: JOB 10 raking band came out thinner, ragged at half-height steps, and partly lost in shading

need: Anchor the chimney through the roof slope into the roof, with a dark masonry role material and a cap course, so it does not float as a pale column.
evidence: JOB 17 flat-topped light-grey column clashes with deepslate and its cap is stuck to a stray roof fragment

need: Default the crow-step depth to at least 2 with a contrasting cap so the stair-stepping reads at glance scale.
evidence: JOB 33 stepped dark cap and crenellations are barely visible and do not add the concept's gable stair-stepping

tool: arch (shapes-curved) for window and door heads
need: Use the arch or segmental hood for window and door openings so the arched profile reads at the detail scale, not just a lintel strip.
evidence: JOB 21 arched ground-floor windows show only a darker lintel strip; JOB 32 side door 'stone arch' shows no arch profile; JOB 35 side window lintels barely change

tool: thin element brush (posts, rails, downpipes; proposed B.post)
need: Place posts, handrails, downpipes and gate posts at a minimum section (2 wide or a capped 1-wide) in a palette role colour, so they read as members rather than sticks or stubs.
evidence: JOB 18 handrails are two small sticks; JOB 24 gate posts are thin stubs; JOB 30 post-and-rail strip is barely visible; JOB 31 downpipe became tan posts in the wrong colour

need: Place planters and shrubs as small volumes (about 3x2 footprint, 2 high) with a leaf or flower palette, so they read as planting at glance scale.
evidence: JOB 22 planters are a few tiny dark-green and purple specks, too small to read as shrubs or flower beds

need: Offer a louvre vent with alternating slats and dark gaps, so the vent reads as a vent rather than a faint plank streak.
evidence: JOB 14 tower-head vent change is a faint lighter-plank streak with no profile or depth

tool: window grid / mullion preset for glass faces
need: Offer a mullion grid preset for glass panes (spacing, frame material, depth) so the glass shaft reads as crisp mullions instead of flat dark glass.
evidence: JOB 26 mullion grid is only faintly different from the before state, with flat glass and no crafted depth

tool: palette by role (role to block mapping)
need: Map 'white' or 'quartz' roles to a quartz or white block, and 'accent gold' to a gold block, so trim and bands match the concept colour rather than falling back to light grey.
evidence: JOB 27 quartz cap and bands read as a mismatched thin grey strip instead of white quartz

need: Give lintels, hoods and sills a projection depth and profile option (e.g. depth 1-2 with a stair or slab step), so any rectangular opening gets a surround that casts shade instead of a flat recolour on the wall face.
evidence: JOB 6 (west hood stub and sill barely read), JOB 7 (lintels are thin dark slabs with no hood profile or depth), JOB 9 (jambs add no visible depth)

need: Add a mullion/glazing-bar option to any window opening (cross or vertical bars in a chosen frame block) so panes read as divided windows, not blank panels.
evidence: JOB 10 glazing change gave flat pale panes with almost no mullion detail

tool: cornice / parapet coping / string course (detailing cornice <F>, cornice, coping)
need: Give cornices, coping and storey string courses a projection depth of at least 2 with a dentil or corbel rhythm option, and a preset that places a string course at every storey line; the current default projects too little to read at elevation scale.
evidence: JOB 7 (eave ledge nearly invisible), JOB 8 (belt courses faint), JOB 10 (roof coping barely visible), JOB 12 (heavy dentilled cornice and string course not produced)

tool: render views for small features (elevation scale)
need: Render a close-up crop around each detail job's target cells, so 1-2 block features (finials, lanterns, flagpoles, shrubs in front of them) are visible to the judge and the builder.
evidence: JOB 14 (finial a faint spike), JOB 17 (flagpole a single block, barely visible), JOB 24 (lantern a dot, half-buried in foliage)

need: Deterministic vertical-element brush: a pole with an optional cap or ball, placed on any apex or roof point, with height and width scaled to the feature so it reads as a finial, flagpole or post at normal viewing distance.
evidence: JOB 14 (pediment finial too small), JOB 17 (tower flagpole one block), JOB 24 (lantern posts at plinth ends unreadable)

need: Place a potted tree or shrub prop (pot block plus leaf or sapling mass, at least 2 blocks tall) into a named bay or corner, so it reads as a plant and not as a green sliver.
evidence: JOB 25 (two thin green strips read as slivers, not potted trees)

need: When a paint or detail rule writes zero cells, fail loudly with the reason (e.g. skipped as already detailed) and offer force as the default for cells a job explicitly targets; never report success on a zero-cell write.
evidence: JOB 13 (pediment rake changed no pixels), JOB 20 (entrance doors no pixels), JOB 36 (edge piers no pixels). Session notes: paint skipped already-detailed cells (0 written); weather rule wrote 0 cells on stone_bricks roof face

need: Apply an arch or segmental head to an existing rectangular ground-floor window or door opening in place, without rebuilding the wall around it.
evidence: JOB 28 (ground windows show no arched heads), JOB 38 (side door arch shows only a faint grey patch)

need: Deterministic classical capital and base brush for pilasters and columns (a 1-2 block capital and plinth step) that fits any column or pilaster width, so the column heads and bases read as ornamented, not as plain shafts.
evidence: JOB 9 (pilaster capitals and bases not readable), JOB 12 (portico capitals only a faint lighter band)

need: Add a contrast-strength and mottling-density parameter to the vary and weather rules, with a visible preset, so stone and deepslate variation reads at elevation scale.
evidence: JOB 1 (north facade texture barely perceptible), JOB 2 (west cracked-deepslate mottling barely registers)

need: Report a per-job pixel-delta measure and a close-up before/after crop, so the judge can tell 'changed but too small' from 'changed nothing' and stops reading small deltas as neutral.
evidence: Most neutral detail jobs (JOB 9, 10, 25, 28) look identical before and after at elevation scale; the judge cannot separate these from no-ops

need: Place a raised-panel tablet with inset, legible lettering on a wall band, keeping its frame, panel relief and clearance from adjacent posts or signs.
evidence: JOB 3 INSPECTORATE plaque: raised carved panels became flat pale stone plus dark blocks and a wood post cutting the sign band; reads patchy, not a plaque.

need: Default to a grounded, stepped finial seated on a roof or pediment cell with no air gap; a 1-block rod off a roof edge must not be an option.
evidence: JOB 7: thin stone rods float at roof corners and pediment feet, reading as antennae with some hovering off the eave.

need: Flag detail blocks with no supporting neighbour or no owning role (floating rods, protruding stubs, stray patches) before render.
evidence: JOB 7 floating finials; JOB 35 stray protruding cornice stubs; JOB 12 stray tan blocks on white piers; JOB 24 stray pale block.

tool: mcd render (banner / entity blocks in glance views)
need: Make placed banners visible in the standard front and front-left close-ups, or report that they are not rendered.
evidence: JOB 11: teal corner banners do not appear in front or front-left close-ups; only a tan block change shows.

tool: downpipe (vertical run, gutter to ground; proposed: B.downpipe)
need: Run a continuous vertical pipe in a chosen material down a pier or corner from roof edge to ground, with a material and tone that match the palette role.
evidence: JOB 12: two tan/terracotta blocks at window height, no vertical run; JOB 33: faint mossy strips barely change the read.

need: Mount a lantern on a bracket projecting from a pier face at a set offset, sized to read at street scale, rather than on a thin chain stub.
evidence: JOB 13: tiny lanterns on a thin dark chain stub, slightly off the pier in the front elevation.

need: Offer a stepped corbelled arch profile over openings with a contrasting voussoir material so the arch reads in the silhouette.
evidence: JOB 15: corbelled arches over shopfront bays show only as faint stair-step notches in the pale stone.

need: Draw mullions in the frame material rather than a tint, so the grid reads on glass at street scale.
evidence: JOB 16: mullion grid shows only faint light-blue lines on the glass.

need: Add transom and sidelight variants for double and single doors, with framing that reads at a glance.
evidence: JOB 17: transom change is tiny and barely shifts the read against the concept's double door.

need: Place potted shrubs or clipped topiary on a plinth or in a planter, with a footprint and height that show from the street.
evidence: JOB 19: potted shrubs and topiary changed no visible pixels in any view.

need: Report each detail job's changed-cell count and visible-pixel delta, and flag jobs that changed nothing as failed rather than as successful edits.
evidence: JOB 18 (entrance steps), JOB 19 (shrubs), JOB 22 (furnishings), JOB 34 (dentil): no pixels changed, with no warning.

need: Include an interior or eye-level view in the default glance set when a job touches interiors, and show single-block changes at a readable scale.
evidence: JOB 22 interior furnishings invisible in exterior views; JOB 24 one-block paving change and JOB 25 moss flecks too small to judge.

tool: relief projection presets (sill <F>, pier, trim, cornice <F>, coping, planter ledges)
need: Default relief projection to at least 2 blocks so sills, pilasters, ledges, coping and eave brackets read at street scale; 1-block defaults vanish.
evidence: JOB 20 planter ledges, JOB 27 pilasters, JOB 36 eave brackets, JOB 39 coping, JOB 35 cornice: thin, barely visible relief.

need: Place shutters flanking the opening outside the glazing, so the glass and mullions stay in place.
evidence: JOB 31: shutters replaced the glazed window with a black void and thin slats, so the windows read as holes.

need: Offer a continuous projecting cornice course with a dentil or bracket rhythm that returns cleanly at corners, with no detached side stubs.
evidence: JOB 35 cornice shows stray stubs at the sides; JOB 36 eave brackets barely visible; JOB 34 dentil row changed no pixels.

need: Give posts a capital and base profile option so a recolour is never the only change to a post.
evidence: JOB 38: arcade posts were only recoloured to a darker, flatter tone with no new profile.

need: Provide a density preset strong enough to read as weathering at building scale, with a visible default.
evidence: JOB 25: moss and cracking show only faint flecks on the plinth; the change is too subtle to register.

tool: palette role-conflict check (proposed: mcd palette check)
need: Flag blocks whose tone breaks their role's contrast (for example light tan on a white pier, or pale blocks on dark stone) before the render.
evidence: JOB 12 tan blocks on white piers; JOB 24 pale weathered block against dark stone.

need: Widening a pier or post to two blocks must keep the wall plane flat and take the wall's own material family, with no stepped or ragged edge, and should refuse a lighter-toned material than the surrounding frame by default.
evidence: JOB 6: widened piers render as pale flat light-oak blocks with a ragged stepped edge on the right pier, clashing with the darker concept tone.

tool: glance render and per-job visibility report
need: Each detail job should report how many judged-view pixels or cells actually changed, and jobs below a visibility floor should be flagged as invisible at glance scale instead of shown as neutral changes.
evidence: JOB 8, 11, 15, 16, 19, 25, 26, 37: before/after renders are nearly identical or the change is too small to read, so the judge cannot tell whether the job helped or hurt.

need: A shutter treatment that builds a panel-shaped closed shutter sized to the window opening (louvred or panelled, with a visible gap at the frame edge), rather than thin full-height slats.
evidence: JOB 14: the 'shutters' render as two thin vertical brown slats running full window height, so the opening reads as dark and empty.

need: Lanterns hung from a pier, bracket or overhang should attach through a chain or bracket to a solid support, align to the building's existing lantern row, and use the build's lantern type; the helper should refuse a placement with no support or an offset from the row.
evidence: JOB 15: one hanging lantern reads as a stray floating block at the edge. JOB 23: a second bracket and lantern sit on a different level and are offset from the existing lantern, forming a cluttered duplicate pair.

need: Before a detail job is accepted, check that new accent blocks (lanterns, caps, rods, gold or copper trim) belong to the build's palette family and flag any hue that clashes with the existing accent.
evidence: JOB 16: gold caps read as odd yellow blocks. JOB 23: cyan soul lantern clashes with the warm lantern palette. JOB 34: bright orange copper cap does not match the dark slate roof.

need: The arch helper should offer a stepped or corbelled head over a rectangular bay, with an optional keystone block, so shopfront and door heads can match a stepped-arch concept.
evidence: JOB 19: arch heads over shopfront bays are a small grey block, not the stepped-arch profile. JOB 26: the gold keystone is not visible because no keystone option exists.

tool: post / colonnade helper with base and capital
need: A post or colonnade treatment should build a column with a base and capital, keep clear of attached lanterns and banners, and avoid a flat slab-like silhouette.
evidence: JOB 31: flat near-black posts stick out of the side return as a bare slab, with unfinished gaps at the base, and they partly hide the lantern and banner.

tool: stair and step helper with support check (nosed treads, cheeks)
need: A step helper should fill the support course under every tread and cheek, then run a void check that reports see-through holes or unsupported cells in the facade.
evidence: JOB 27: the change opens a see-through hole in the bottom step course and a gap beside the cheek, creating broken voids and a ragged silhouette.

need: A chimney should seat on the local roof plane by extending down to the sloped surface under its footprint, and it should offer a replace-existing mode so the old chimney is removed rather than left beside the new one.
evidence: JOB 34: the new chimney is a wide detached block floating off the roof slope with a visible gap beneath, and the old thin chimney is still standing beside it.

need: A hip-and-gable (irimoya) roof preset with a true gablet on the front or back face, a flat ridge cap, and no ridge spike. The existing `pediment` option makes a flat hip plateau instead of a gablet.
evidence: Builder: no East-Asian roof preset (`temple` is Greek); `pediment` gives a flat-topped hip plateau, not a gablet. Reviewer: 'does not read as a Japanese hip-and-gable'; 'rebuild the gable end as a clean pediment instead of a notch'.

need: An eave option that upswept-tips the corners and eave line with stair/slab courses (a curved or upturned eave), with a tunable kick height. The current `flared` eave kicks only slightly.
evidence: Builder: eave corner tips were hand-placed full blocks; `flared` kicks only slightly. Reviewer: 'no upswept corners'; 'straight eaves'; 'flare the eave corners upward with stair/slab tips'.

need: A `maxHeight` cap, or an auto-pitch that fits span and the 9-block height limit, so builders don't tune numeric pitch by trial renders. This also frees headroom for finials.
evidence: Builder: 9-wide span at 45° overshot the 9-block height limit; pitch tuned by trial renders; `finial` could not be used because the roof hit the height cap.

need: Overhang default or clamp scaled to wall height and span, so the overhang cannot hide most of the wall. The check should warn when the roof covers more than a set fraction of the wall face.
evidence: Reviewer: 'overhang so deep it hides almost the whole wall'; 'pull the roof overhang in by 1 block'. Rejected detail task on the same issue returned no output.

tool: mcd roof (pitch rounding / dutch-gable on narrow spans)
need: Pitch values in the 0.67–1.0 range should round to clean steps, and `dutch-gable` should not produce a tower-like gablet or slab ring on spans under about 10 blocks. Narrow spans need a safe preset default.
evidence: Builder: pitch 0.67–1.0 gives lumpy plateaus and odd rise rounding; `dutch-gable` gave a tower-like gablet and slab ring on a 9×7 span, so it was unusable.

tool: mcd roof (pediment tympanum fill) / mcd roof (gable fill)
need: A pattern option for the gable or pediment tympanum (lattice, kumiko, or timber-frame) so window grids and framing can be generated instead of hand-placed.
evidence: Builder: 'pediment tympanum cannot take a lattice/timber-frame pattern'; kumiko window in the gable was hand-placed trapdoors.

need: A paper-screen brush that lays a pale panel inside dark posts at a set bay spacing, with horizontal rails at top and middle, an optional lattice ranma band, and a sliding-door offset. Works on any panel and frame blocks.
evidence: Builder: 'no brush for paper screens'; panels, posts and ranma were hand-placed. Reviewer: 'shoji screens are not legible'; 'run dark posts every 2 blocks with horizontal rails'; 'continuous shoji bays'.

need: A panel-material option on `glazing grid` so it can frame non-glass panels such as white concrete, snow, or trapdoor lattice.
evidence: Builder: 'glazing grid needs glass, so panels, posts and ranma were hand-placed'; `mullions` was the nearest option.

need: A raised-deck brush with corner and edge posts, an outer rail that leaves a gap for steps, and a continuous footing course under the floor that closes the under-floor gaps. Rails should not repeat as a flat plank band.
evidence: Builder: 'engawa/veranda all hand-placed'; 'raised floor on footings with 1-block gap: nothing'. Reviewer: 'gaps under the floor show as white or empty holes'; 'flat, uniform plank band with repetitive fence-post railing'.

need: A stone lantern brush with base, post, and cap, plus a lantern on top. It should read clearly at a distance and sit beside a path.
evidence: Builder: 'stone lantern (toro) hand-built'. Reviewer: 'stone lantern is just one stone post'; 'give the lantern a base, post and cap'.

need: A red/orange autumn species option for `tree` (maple-like crown), beyond oak, birch, dark_oak, spruce, and azalea. Nether-wart or red-leaf blocks are a possible fallback.
evidence: Builder: 'tree supports only oak/birch/dark_oak/spruce/azalea (no red maple)'. Reviewer: 'the maple is a red cube cluster'; 'reads as a mailbox or signpost, not a tree'.

need: A rounded, layered canopy with irregular gaps, a few hanging leaf blocks, and a gap-free trunk-to-canopy connection. Output should have no floating or orphan leaves.
evidence: Builder: maple canopy needed pruning to remove floating/orphan blocks. Reviewer: 'floating block cluster'; 'gap between canopy and trunk'; 'break the cube silhouette'.

need: A stepping-stone mode for `path` that places staggered slabs on a straight run from a point to a point, instead of dirt_path that follows terrain.
evidence: Builder: `path` 'follows terrain and uses dirt_path; no stepping-stone mode'. Reviewer: 'stepping stones are scattered with no clear path'.

need: A scatter brush for shrubs and bushes (leaf and moss blocks) with a leaf-litter carpet option for ground under trees, placed within a set radius of a building or path.
evidence: Reviewer: 'the garden is sparse'; 'add a few bushes, moss and a small pond or gravel patch'; 'add some fallen-leaf carpet blocks on the grass'.

need: Render white and paper-type blocks (white concrete, wool) at true luminance so they do not appear light grey. The render should match the block's real color for the judge.
evidence: Builder: 'paper white renders light grey in mcd render (white concrete / wool)'; snow_block was the only clean white. Reviewer: 'paper-screen walls barely read'.

need: `mcd palette` should suggest a contrast-safe substitute per role when it flags dark-on-dark or trim-invisible pairs, such as dark oak fence on dark oak log or spruce trim on spruce walls. It should not just flag them.
evidence: Builder: 'dark oak fence invisible on dark oak log background'; 'spruce_planks trim invisible on spruce_planks walls'. Reviewer: 'dark roof, dark timber and dark posts merge into one heavy mass'.

tool: paint vary (deepslate tiles) / roof material mix
need: `paint vary` should write variants for deepslate and dark tile blocks, and roof material should accept a multi-shade mix option so the dark slab breaks up.
evidence: Builder: 'paint vary wrote 0 cells on deepslate tiles'; 'no roof-tile weathering for dark tiles'. Reviewer: 'mix a few tile shades to break up the dark slab'.

need: A projecting porch or wing brush with its own lower roof, or a two-tier eave step, so the massing breaks out of a plain rectangle.
evidence: Reviewer: 'plain rectangle with one roof mass and no offset wing or porch'; 'add a small projecting entry porch with its own lower roof, or step the eave heights'.

need: A check that flags tree or prop cells within N blocks of a building footprint or overlapping a roof edge, so trees are not placed into the building envelope.
evidence: Reviewer: 'maple ... sits partly inside the roof edge'; 'move the maple out into the garden at least 3 blocks from the house'. `mcd check` reported orphan and floating blocks but not clearance.

need: Place a sloped, striped cloth canopy along any frontage run: stairs rising toward the wall, posts at a set spacing, a valance edge, and a stripe-colour option. The canopy must attach to the wall or posts so it does not float.
evidence: Builder hand-placed a sloped striped awning in a loop (closest tool is bunting, which is banners only). Reviewer: 'floating awning frame' and 'awning edges ragged where they overlap the viga ends'.

need: Place clusters of small props (pots, baskets, barrels, crates, hay bales) at a chosen base or frontage, sized to read from street distance. Include a grouping/clumping option and a preset per building type.
evidence: Builder hand-placed decorated_pot, barrel, hay_block and composter. Reviewer: 'clay pots and baskets are small and hard to read at street view'. planter only does window boxes and raised beds.

need: Build a thick-walled shell from any footprint polygon, with a chamfer or rounded-corner option and a wall-thickness parameter, so walls are not composed from overlapping rectangles.
evidence: Builder looped over two overlapping rectangles to get rounded corners and a 2-wall shell. Reviewer: 'walls look thin and square-edged, not thick and rounded like adobe'. shell is rectangular only.

need: Place protruding beam ends on an even rhythm under a parapet or eave line. Options: log type, protrusion depth, spacing, and face selection. It should also flag or refuse strays that are not attached to a wall.
evidence: Builder hand-placed log stubs on all four sides. Reviewer: 'oversized dark-oak cubes', 'floating one at right', 'strays on the tower and back corners'. brackets only does stairs and slabs.

need: Give dome a smooth silhouette at small radii (r<=3), using a stair/slab ring profile that does not step like a pyramid, and a course-band option (for example an orange band) like cylinder's bands.
evidence: Builder: 'Dome profiles at radius 3 on a flat deck read as a stepped pyramid'. Reviewer: 'lumpy sand-block dome... reads as a pyramid or sand pile'. dome has no band option.

need: Set a coping material separate from the deck material, and apply railing or a parapet to selected sides only, with a railing height that stops at the parapet top.
evidence: Builder used paint railing rules with explicit x ranges because roof had no per-side railing or coping option. Reviewer: 'fence posts poke above the parapet'. Also 'deck's mud-brick slab merges with the coping'.

need: Default to a continuous parapet around the full roof edge with consistent crenellation on every side. A per-side override should be explicit, not the result of partial calls.
evidence: Reviewer: 'the parapet is thin and patchy, with the crenellation present on only some sides' and 'a continuous slab or wall parapet around the whole roof edge'.

need: Treat doors as passable openings, count doorsteps outside the box, and take a street-edge parameter. End-to-end walk along an axis should then be reported correctly.
evidence: Builder: 'check circulation treats doors as walls and ignores doorsteps outside the box, so end-to-end along x reported false even with side doors'. Also 'minClearWidth=4 on x-axis' flagged.

need: Let the builder declare a monochrome-by-design palette, and classify trim as invisible only when its contrast with the adjacent face is below a threshold. Intentional accent stripes should not be flagged as outliers.
evidence: Builder: 'flags the intentional white quartz awning stripes as outliers' and 'flags sandstone-on-sandstone trim in a monochrome desert palette'. Trim-invisible and dark-on-dark flags recurred across several checks.

need: Either mutate the grid in place or name the call so it is clearly non-mutating. Returning a copy silently drops edits when called like a mutating brush.
evidence: Builder: '`paint` returns a COPY (grid in `.grid`); easy to lose the railing by calling it like a mutating brush'.

need: Restrict weathering and variation to the same material family (sandstone: cut, smooth, chiseled only). Stop them from introducing diorite, calcite or dripstone speckle.
evidence: Builder: 'Weather/vary on sandstone produced diorite/calcite/dripstone speckle'. The builder disabled the pass instead of getting a family-safe result.

need: Support a one-block-high sign band between an awning and a beam line, with a flanking-sign placement on a facade.
evidence: Builder: 'Wall signs... could not fit a 1-cell-high band between awning and viga' and fell back to hand-placed B.sign.

need: Cut evenly spaced vent slots into the faces of a tower or shaft, with a slot-width and spacing option and a stepped cap.
evidence: Builder: 'filled a 3x3 shaft and placed vents by hand'. Reviewer: 'Give the wind tower open vent slots'.

need: Offer an axis-centring helper so a dome or tower is centred on the entrance axis or a named facade centre. Off-centre placement should be an explicit choice.
evidence: Reviewer: 'the dome sits off-centre against the wind tower' and 'tower and dome sit off-centre without a clear relationship to the entrance'.

need: Report elevations whose opening count or relief is below a threshold, per face, so a blank side or back wall is flagged before the render review.
evidence: Reviewer: 'The back and side walls are flat bands... no openings or relief, so they read as blank'. Current checks did not flag this.

need: Render each block with its true texture and opacity. Flag any block that renders translucent or untextured, so a reviewer does not mistake a palette change for a glass or artifact result.
evidence: Rejected task: after-view 'replaces the sandstone bands with translucent pinkish-grey panels that read as glass or a rendering artifact'. The cause is unconfirmed; it may be a block or texture fault rather than a design choice.

need: Accept a per-layer block list (or a repeating band pattern with arbitrary blocks) so a striped round shaft is one call, not one call per band.
evidence: Builder called cylinder once per colour band; the reviewer's Major Massing issue asked for red/white bands carried around a curved wall.

need: Build a shallow cone or low-pitch cap with a small eave overhang, raised on posts over a glazed lantern drum, with a finial and optional light block.
evidence: Reviewer: the lantern cap reads as a flat black lid or an onion/helmet dome. The roof presets do not cover lantern caps.

need: Default a dome to a cone or low-pitch profile for caps and finials, and warn when a bulb or onion profile sits on a small drum.
evidence: Reviewer: the bulbous black cap reads as an onion dome. The cap used a bulb-like shape where a cone was wanted.

need: Build a glazed drum: a ring of glass panes with mullions, an iron-bar or fence frame, and a central lamp block that stays visible from outside.
evidence: Builder hand-placed a ring of glass, iron bars and glowstone. Reviewer: the lantern room is mostly open posts, so the light reads as a small block.

need: Frame openings (door, window, sill, lintel) on a curved wall at the true cardinal and radial positions, not only on flat faces.
evidence: Builder hand-placed tower window and door frames on a round wall. Reviewer: tower window slits are narrow, irregular and stacked in a column.

tool: openings schedule on a curved shaft (proposed option on cylinder or surround)
need: Place windows at an even or staggered vertical rhythm around a shaft, with optional stone sills, from one spec.
evidence: Reviewer: window slits stack in a column and need staggering or sills. Builder placed them by hand.

need: Connect fence and railing blocks (not only *_wall) around a circular gallery so the railing reads as continuous.
evidence: Builder wrote fence connection states by hand because ring connects only walls. Reviewer: the gallery looks empty.

need: Build an upside-down stair or slab corbel course around a circle with facing computed per cell, not by a dominant-axis rule, so diagonals are not jagged.
evidence: Builder hand-placed a corbelled gallery under a round tower with jagged diagonals. Reviewer: the gallery floor and cap stack into a dark slab.

need: Mirror a finished region (including stair shape, facing, door hinge and fence keys), not only writes made inside the callback.
evidence: Builder wrote its own mirror because mirrorX only mirrors writes inside its callback. Symmetric cottage front detail was needed.

tool: porch awning and shutters (proposed: awning, shutter)
need: Place a porch awning (stairs on fence posts), paired shutters (open trapdoors) and a window-box planter in one call, with the glass set back from the wall.
evidence: Builder hand-placed all three. Reviewer: door and porch read weakly at street view, and the cottage front is dark and cluttered.

need: Work on curved walls, so a door sign or pennant can sit on a cylinder face without manual placement.
evidence: Builder did not build the door sign or pennant because plaque and signboard fail on curved walls.

need: Clip or keep the roof against an existing adjacent mass (for example a tower wall) so a pre-built curved wall does not need to be built after the roof.
evidence: Builder had to build the tower wall after the cottage roof so the cylinder overwrote the buried roof end. Reviewer: the cottage roof runs up the tower wall and reads as a mess.

need: Place a chimney on the ridge or gable end with a flue, campfire or lantern top, and flag a floating chimney stub with no supporting wall.
evidence: Chimney was a 2x2 with no flue or top. Reviewer: a floating chimney stub and a grey stone stub beside the tower.

need: Join a small house to a curved tower with a short link or doorway, so the house stands clear with its own ridge instead of jamming into the shaft.
evidence: Reviewer: the cottage is a tiny lean-to jammed against the tower wall, not a separate small house.

need: Run the floating-block and orphan check on the exported build as a gate, and flag floating slabs at the rear and sides as well as the front.
evidence: Reviewer: floating grey slab fragments hang beside the tower and the rear of the cottage has stray blocks. The build passed a check run on an earlier version.

need: Scatter grass in clumps or use moss and vine accents by default, not scattered bright grass squares.
evidence: Reviewer: the base has scattered bright grass squares that read as noise. Minor Finish.

tool: rock outcrop with cut-in stair (proposed: outcrop)
need: Build a rock island with a stepped stair flight cut into it, with moss and fern cover, as one preset rather than a hand-written height loop.
evidence: Builder hand-wrote a height loop for a rocky outcrop. heightfield and strata are for valleys, not rock islands.

need: Stacked tiers where each setback volume takes its own steep gable or hip roof with a chosen ridge axis and a shrinking footprint, so tiers read as separate stacked roofs, not one lid.
evidence: Stacked tiers (nave, clerestory, belfry) built wall-by-wall by hand; setbacks has no per-tier steep roof or ridge-axis choice. Reviewer: lower roof is a lid, upper tiers sit on it, ground floor is a low wide box.

tool: mcd roof (eave overhang and shingle courses)
need: A roof option that adds a clear eave overhang and alternating stair/slab shingle courses with an optional trim line under the eave, so the roof shows shingle rows and an eave line.
evidence: Dark-on-dark deepslate with no courses, texture or eave line. Reviewer asked for alternating deepslate_tile stairs and slabs with a stripped-spruce eave trim.

tool: mcd roof (steep pitch on small footprints)
need: Steep pitch presets that stay proportionate on small footprints (a 3x3 belfry) and produce a tall, slender, shingled spire rather than a needle.
evidence: steep pyramid on a 3x3 belfry gave a thin needle. Reviewer: spire and cross finial are small; wants a tall slender shingled needle.

need: A flared-base (broach) spire option on tower: spire that transitions from a square tower to an octagonal or conical spire.
evidence: Builder wanted a broach option on tower: spire; pyramid gave a straight needle with no flare at the base.

need: A profile brush that builds a compact 3-4 block curved neck with an upswept beak from stairs, logs and trapdoors, anchored at a ridge or gable peak and mirrored across gable ends.
evidence: Dragon heads hand-placed via dragon() in build.mjs; no curved ornament tool exists (finial is straight only). Reviewer: loose brown blocks and curls float on roof edges, read as stray prongs.

need: Gable and ridge ornaments default to anchoring at ridge-end peaks, not on roof slopes, with a mirror option for paired ornaments.
evidence: Dragon heads sat on roof slopes rather than gable peaks. Reviewer: place as mirrored pairs at the ridge ends of each tier.

need: A brush that builds an open arcade ring around a core: evenly spaced posts, a rail or lattice between them, a gap to the inner wall, and a beam line.
evidence: Gallery (svalgang) ring built by hand around the core. Reviewer: evenly spaced plank pillars read as a warehouse wall; wants an open arcade with a gap to the inner wall and a base plinth.

tool: mcd roof (skirt / lean-to over a taller core)
need: A skirt or lean-to roof style that wraps a taller core and meets its wall, built from the core footprint outward, without building a hip over the full plan and carving it out.
evidence: Builder built a hip over the whole plan and carved it out to make the gallery lean-to roof. Reviewer: the lean-to roof over the arcade needs a shingled finish.

tool: glazing grid (gable triangles and louvre windows)
need: Glazing and louvre options that apply inside gable triangles and on belfry walls, not only on flat facades.
evidence: glazing grid works on flat facades but not inside gable triangles. Builder hand-placed lattice windows; reviewer wanted a louvred belfry in place of the see-through hole.

tool: timber-framed gable end (bargeboards and exposed beams)
need: A timber-framed gable brush with bargeboards, exposed tie beams and a symmetrical crossed-beam pattern, distinct from classical pediments.
evidence: pediment is classical (quartz-style cornice); no timber gable exists. Reviewer asked for symmetrical crossed-beam gable ends with bargeboards.

tool: diagonal brace brush (St Andrew's crosses, rafter ends)
need: A brush that places diagonal braces and crossed timber members on a facade or gable, with a choice of X or Z pattern.
evidence: Timber framing hand-placed. pilasters profile timber is vertical only. Reviewer: stave and St Andrew's crosses wanted.

need: A timber facade preset with a regular rhythm (vertical stripped logs with a trim rail) as default, so the output is not a mix of stair and plank shapes.
evidence: Upper timber section is a jumble of stair and plank shapes with noisy detail. Reviewer: replace with a regular pattern of vertical stripped logs and a trim rail.

need: A signboard or hanging-sign option that attaches to a post or beam, usable when the porch is open on several sides.
evidence: B.sign gave an unsupported-attachment warning when placed in the wall cell. signboard was not usable because the porch is open on three sides.

need: A finial cross preset that sets fence connection states automatically, so the cross arms link without manual state setting.
evidence: B.fence has no connected form; fence connection states set by hand for the cross finial. Reviewer: spire and cross finial too small.

need: A brush that adds a half-cylinder or polygonal apse to one end of a box, with its roof stepping down from the nave.
evidence: Reviewer: add a lower chancel or apse at one end and step roof heights down toward the ends. Not expressible with the existing cylinder brush alone.

need: Stepped roof tiers default to a continuous eave edge at each tier join, with no crenellated jags or corner stubs.
evidence: Roof edges crenellated and jagged where tiers meet; stray block stubs at the corners. Reviewer asked for a continuous stair or slab eave edge.

need: An mcd check that flags unintended see-through holes in a facade or tower wall when viewed from an elevation.
evidence: Reviewer saw a see-through hole in the upper tower on the back elevation; mcd check reported orphans but no elevation through-hole finding.

need: A base-course preset that breaks a large blank stone base with a stair course, a cobble/mossy mix and a plinth step, applied as one call.
evidence: Stone base large, blank and flat. plinth <F> exists in detailing.md but was not used; builder left the base blank. Reviewer wants a stair/slab course and a cobble/mossy mix.

need: Flat roofs with an overhang need a slim slab (1 block, selectable), an optional light fascia or rim band, and a soffit course (timber or stone) under the overhang, all as options instead of hand-placed.
evidence: Builder: flat-parapet gives only a 1-2 course parapet and slab coping; fascia ring, soffit and deck were placed by hand. Reviewer: roof reads as a thick dark lid with no fascia edge and no visible soffit.

need: Per-side overhang (or eave width per face) so a roof can cantilever over chosen sides only, without the builder widening the whole footprint by hand.
evidence: Builder: overhang on 2 sides only (1 elsewhere); roof() takes one footprint, so the footprint was widened by hand. Reviewer: overhang is shallow and the terrace side is unsheltered.

need: A curtain-wall brush that lays a bay rhythm of glass panels between slim posts (mullions) with head and sill rails, full storey height, on any face of a plan.
evidence: Builder: no curtain-wall brush; posts placed by hand. Reviewer (x2): brief's floor-to-ceiling glass not visible; glass shows only as small panes between black piers; side and back walls blank.

need: Thin glass panes must be visible at the render scale used by the judge, or the renderer/judge should flag that thin glazing is invisible rather than letting the build pass.
evidence: Builder: glass_pane is invisible at render scale, so full glass blocks were used instead. Reviewer: glazing reads as small mullioned panes only.

need: Glazing grid applied to new bays (not only existing walls), with a floor-to-ceiling mode and a pane-to-pier ratio option.
evidence: Builder: glazing brush works on existing walls only. Reviewer: back and side walls remain blank planes.

need: Louvre or vent panel that works on a plain solid wall, not only on glass.
evidence: Builder: louvres needs glass; no louvre option works on a plain wall, so the plant-room vent was abandoned.

need: Furniture brush that places tables and chairs on a grid (one table with N chairs per set), counters and stools, with chair facing set by the table direction.
evidence: Builder: no table/chair brush; fence+trapdoor tables and stair chairs placed by hand, and chair facing (stair back) needed a fix. Reviewer: tables and chairs are a jumble of stairs and trapdoors; spacing uneven.

need: Glowing block-letter sign option for short panels (about 4 rows) with a dark backing and light outline, or a projecting or free-standing sign mode.
evidence: Builder: plaque gives flat orange letters; block font needs 5+ rows plus margin. Reviewer (x2): CAFE sign is small, low, hidden by planters, and reads as paint rather than a neon sign.

need: Glass or post-and-glass railing along any plinth or flat-top edge, with a configurable gap for steps and matching corner posts.
evidence: Builder: no railing brush for a glass balustrade with a step gap; terrace screens and posts placed by hand. Reviewer: glass railing is very thin; corner posts look oversized or like stray cubes.

need: Steps brush that adds a half-height or full approach course to a plinth edge, centred on a chosen face.
evidence: Builder: entry steps on the plinth placed by hand; no steps brush for plinths.

need: Recessed downlight option that places a light block flush in a soffit or ceiling course at a set spacing.
evidence: Builder: glowstone placed in the soffit by hand; the palette flags it as an outlier.

tool: mcd check (unsupported-lantern rule) / palette outlier flag
need: Allow sea_lantern as a lantern in check, and let deliberate light accents (role: light) pass the palette outlier flag.
evidence: Builder: sea_lantern flagged as an unsupported lantern by check; palette flags glowstone downlights as outliers.

need: Hanging lanterns that anchor their chain to a block above (roof underside or beam) and space evenly under an edge.
evidence: Builder: lanterns on chains placed without support. Reviewer: lanterns float without visible support in the back view and look loose.

need: Planter box option for tall hedges (leaf-block hedge in a planter), not only beds and window boxes.
evidence: Builder: tall hedge in a planter box placed by hand; planter brush only does beds and window boxes.

need: Paving brush that lays a patterned surface with a 2-tone border or inset strip across a rectangular area.
evidence: Reviewer: terrace is a flat light-grey slab; wants a 2-tone border or inset strip. Builder notes do not mention paving, so this is inferred from the reviewer.

need: A build-level option to design in street coordinates (front, left, right), so mirrored or viewer-left designs do not need a custom put/fill wrapper.
evidence: Builder: mirrored (viewer-left) design needed a custom X(u)/put wrapper beyond mirrorX.

need: Dormers must work on steep pyramid, cone and hip roofs, or the result must say which dormer was dropped and why (e.g. 'roof surface below dormer sill').
evidence: dormers:[{face:'north'}] on a pyramid silently produced nothing across gable/shed, row 0/2 and width 1/3 variants; builder hand-cut the dormer. Reviewer: 'dormer poking out' / 'dormer sits awkwardly'.

need: A tall, smooth cone or steep spire on a rect or round footprint, with per-ring centre offset (lean) and taper to a point, without stair-step lumps.
evidence: Pyramid is a square-stepped, centred, broad form; reviewer wanted 'a tall crooked wizard's cone', 'lean barely visible'. A rejected cone attempt read as 'a tall ragged green mass with irregular stair-step protrusions'.

need: Preset for a tall narrow roof (steep pitch, overhang 1) so the default does not produce a wide shallow lid; presets should match the named style.
evidence: Builder kept a broad pyramid with a wide eave; reviewer: 'reads like a lid on a box', 'shrink the eave overhang to 1 block'. Pitch was also reduced to 1.5 to fix grid overflow.

need: A dry run that reports the resulting height, footprint growth and grid overflow for a style/pitch/grow setting before any blocks are written.
evidence: grow:false caused a fit error on a pyramid overhang; grow:true silently grew the grid; height was only found by trial (cupola cap exceeded y=16).

need: Chimney rise measured from the local roof surface, and an option to anchor the chimney to the roof slope with a base and steps.
evidence: rise is relative to the roof apex, so a chimney at the eave towered over the roof; a negative rise was needed. Reviewer: 'chimney floats beside the roof with a visible gap', 'stuck on'.

need: A jetty / overhanging-storey brush that places the cantilever and its brackets on chosen faces in one call.
evidence: Each storey and its upside-down stair brackets were placed by hand. Reviewer: 'jettied floors' only read through a small jetty.

need: Per-storey x/z offset, rotation and taper, so upper storeys shift, narrow or turn relative to the storey below.
evidence: Reviewer (x2): 'square symmetric box', 'offset each upper storey by a block or two', 'taper the stone shaft', 'upper floors look like a separate cottage perched on a stone chimney'.

need: A half-timber wall brush that lays posts, sills, knee or cross bracing and plaster infill in bays, with window cut-outs, so large plaster fields are broken up by construction.
evidence: Plaster, log posts, knee braces and round windows were all hand-looped. Reviewer: 'large flat white panels'. Closest tools (surround timber, pilasters) do not cover bracing or infill.

need: A round or octagonal window option with a ring frame around a glass centre, sized to read as round at street distance.
evidence: Only a pediment oculus exists. Reviewer: 'small round windows read as square glass panes', 'make the windows round by building ring-shaped frames'.

need: A balcony brush that places a deck of a set depth, a full rail on the chosen face, and support brackets, with the depth as a parameter.
evidence: Deck, fence ring and stair brackets were hand-placed. Reviewer: 'balcony and telescope are tiny and lost', 'extend to a 2-block platform with a full fence rail'. Closest is the railing treatment, which covers the top only.

need: Small free-standing props (a tube on a stand or bracket) that are attached to a support and read as the named object at street distance.
evidence: No prop library; closest was lightning_rod + fence. Rejected task: 'telescope is now a black slab that floats past the wall with no visible support'.

need: An ivy/vine treatment that places vine blocks and leaf tufts on chosen wall faces with strand continuation and clustering.
evidence: Ivy was a hand loop with clustering. Closest was vary/gradient, which only swaps blocks.

need: A height-field mound or rock plinth brush with stepped access and one consistent cobble/moss mix, sized for small plinths (about 13x13).
evidence: Hand-written height-field loop. Reviewer: 'stone base platform is noisy and irregular', 'base has scattered grass and moss blocks'. Landscaping brushes did not fit a tiny plinth.

need: A default that gives a consistent cobble-to-moss ratio with clumping, instead of scattered single blocks.
evidence: Reviewer: 'scattered grass and moss blocks', 'trim stray mossy blocks on the base platform'.

need: Hanging lanterns that attach under any overhang or jetty underside, not only facades found by face maps, with even spacing along the eave line.
evidence: Builder: 'fixtures at eaves only works on facades found by face maps and could not reach the jetty corners'. Reviewer: 'lanterns are sparse and hang on odd chains'.

need: Render a glow halo for light-emitting blocks (glass with a light source, shroomlight, glowstone) so a lit window can be judged as lit.
evidence: Stained glass rendered pale/pink with no light engine; builder placed shroomlight in the glass to make it read as lit. Reviewer: 'the glowing window is just a small orange patch'.

need: On an already-framed opening, either replace the frame with an explicit option, or name the force keyword in the 'already detailed' message.
evidence: mcd paint surround on an already-framed door reported 'already detailed' and wrote 0 cells; the force keyword was only found by trial.

need: A vertical-circulation brush that routes a ladder or stair through several floors and adds backing blocks at each floor where wall lines shift.
evidence: Builder hand-placed backing blocks at each floor of a multi-storey shaft because the wall lines shift with the jetties.

need: Facade rhythm (window slits, buttresses, lanterns) applied to every face of a building, not only the faces that face maps describe.
evidence: Reviewer: 'the rear stone shaft is a blank wall with only a couple of odd blocks', 'add a window slit, buttress or ivy streaks and a lantern on the back stone shaft'.

need: A roof preset that takes a footprint, a ridge axis and a ridge count, and builds repeating sloped copper backs with vertical glazed faces on the same side, plus a continuous parapet, without hand-chaining shed calls.
evidence: Reviewer: roof reads as a flat lid, not a sawtooth. Builder: had to chain roof() shed over three rects and hand-glaze the steps; 'no sawtooth option'.

need: A glazing option that puts glass into the sloped roof surface as a strip or per-bay panel, so skylights are part of the roof rather than a hand edit.
evidence: Builder: 'Sloped skylight strip (glass in the roof surface): no option; needs a hand edit.' Reviewer: skylights are not distinct.

need: When a slope is requested in a full block like copper_block, either pick the cut_ stair/slab variant automatically or warn, so the slope has no gaps.
evidence: Builder: 'shed with copper_block silently gave a gappy slope (no stair/slab variant).'

tool: roof material choice by palette role
need: Roof presets and sawtooth/skylight variants should draw their material from the palette role and check contrast with the walls and glazing, so a new roof material does not clash or hide glass.
evidence: Rejected task: grey sawtooth blocks 'clash with the oxidized copper' and hide the glass skylights in the front view.

tool: mcd roof: continuous parapet / edge closure
need: A parapet option that runs continuously around the whole footprint and checks that the roof-to-wall join has no gap at any corner.
evidence: Reviewer: parapet at front-left leaves a gap and the roof edge is ragged at the back.

need: A brush that builds a round window or gear: outer ring of a chosen block, inner glass disc, optional N spokes and a hub, and optional teeth. Should sit on a wall plane and be centred over an opening.
evidence: Reviewer: gear window reads as damage, not a gear; 'big round gear window is not readable'. Builder: no circular window brush; placed disc, ring and teeth by hand with a distance test.

need: A brush that lays continuous pipe runs along a wall or roof with bends, joints and a valve block (lever, button or wheel) at each bend, in a chosen block.
evidence: Reviewer: pipes and valves are a few stray rods and dots. Builder: no pipe brush; used copper blocks and grindstone as a valve by hand.

need: A brush that builds a projecting jib or beam from a wall with a hoist, a hanging chain and a hook, sized relative to the opening below it.
evidence: Reviewer: crane arm and hoist not legible, nothing above the loading door. Builder: 'Crane / gantry / jib: nothing.'

need: Lantern fixtures should take a material option (copper, iron, spruce) and hang from a chain or bracket, instead of defaulting to spruce or iron.
evidence: Builder: hanging lantern in fixture defaults to spruce/iron; had to hand-place copper_lantern.

need: A chimney brush that rises from a roof or a wall plane to a chosen height, with banded courses and a flared or stepped cap, so tall stacks need no hand caps.
evidence: Reviewer: chimneys are short, plain and flat-topped. Builder: 'roof --chimney can only sit on a roof, not rise from a wall plane'; hand-built caps.

need: A brush that adds a lean-to or bay projection off one wall, with its own roof pitch and an optional loading opening, so a plain box gets a side annex.
evidence: Reviewer: plain cube with little projection and no side annex or bay. Stave church builder also added a lean-to roof by hand.

need: A check that flags wall or roof cells where the interior is visible from outside or sky shows through the shell, reported by face and coordinates.
evidence: Reviewer: right wall largely open with holes showing interior and sky; front face see-through; back wall has a void. Existing orphan/floating checks did not catch these.

need: Circulation check should accept door-to-door routes (or a chosen entrance pair) instead of assuming a corridor along the long axis, so closed buildings don't report false.
evidence: Builder: 'mcd check circulation ... reports false for every closed building; needs a door-to-door mode.'

need: A surround option that only recesses or frames openings and leaves the wall material alone, so plinth-height walls do not turn grey.
evidence: Builder: 'surround preset plain on a plinth-height wall turns the whole lower wall grey; no recess-only option.'

need: A mirror tool that works on a finished build and flips stair, door, pane and facing state correctly, not just inside a paint function.
evidence: Builder: 'Mirroring a finished build (with stair/door/pane state flips) was not available: wrote mirrorGrid() by hand; mirrorX only works inside a paint function.'

tool: fins / bands: regular horizontal bands and riveted panels
need: A banding option that places copper or metal bands and rivet panels at a regular spacing across a wall, instead of random patches.
evidence: Reviewer: copper accent patches on brick walls are random and unframed; wants ordered horizontal bands or riveted panels at regular spacing.

need: Default a continuous plinth to the full footprint at the base and check it, so loose stone stubs and a ragged base are not left behind.
evidence: Reviewer: loose stone stubs at the base; asked for a continuous stone plinth. Builder had orphan and floating cleanup but not a base plinth.

need: A gambrel/barn preset with a steep lower slope, shallow upper slope, visible break line, eave overhang and ridge cap, so builders don't hand-tune pitch, lower and upperPitch.
evidence: No barn preset (only granary). Builder overrode to gambrel with pitch 1.5, lower 2, upperPitch 0.34, found by reading roofs.mjs. Roof reads as one flat black slab with no break line.

need: Overhang that stays inside the declared footprint by trimming the body, or a fixed-grid mode, so eaves and barge boards are possible without growing the grid or shifting coordinates.
evidence: Overhang grew the grid 15x17x21 to 17x17x22 and shifted coordinates. Builder forced overhang 0, losing the eave. grow:false was too restrictive for a pyramid overhang. Cupola cap went past y=16.

need: Eave brackets or corbels that attach to a wall face without requiring a roof overhang.
evidence: Dark stair corbels under the eave were not possible at overhang 0, because brackets need an overhang to hang under.

need: Height control for pyramid and spire roofs independent of footprint, with a finial that seats on the apex block automatically.
evidence: Wizard tower got a broad pyramid where a tall spire was wanted. Pitch was cut to 1.5 to avoid grid overflow. The finial floated until an apex block was added by hand.

need: Dormers that accept several faces in one call (symmetric east and west), and report a dropped dormer instead of dropping it silently.
evidence: dormers takes one face per call, so the concept's three per side could not be expressed. On a pyramid roof that does not rise over them, all dormer variants dropped silently.

need: A cupola brush: louvred shaft, pitched cap that does not add height, and a fence-and-banner or arrow vane, sized to a given footprint.
evidence: Louvres and shaft hand-built. Cap roof() added layers. No weathervane brush (finial has no arrow, tower top is hollow). Cupola nearly invisible from front; vane a thin line.

need: A door-leaf brush: flat panel, diagonal X brace in stairs or slabs, centre seam and rail, with a rule for leaf widths so the X does not read as a checker.
evidence: X hand-written as diagonal cells on a 4x4 leaf. Half the cells made it read as a red-and-white checkerboard.

need: A hoist brush: beam projecting past a gable or wall face, with bracket, chain, and a hanging load (bale or lantern).
evidence: Logs, stair bracket, iron_chain and hay bale all placed by hand. Closest existing tool is attach lantern. Bale flagged as orphan.

need: Prop-group scatter (bale stacks, barrel groups) and a fence-run brush that works on grade and stops at a path gap, not only on roof tops.
evidence: Bale stacks, barrels and fence with path gap all hand-placed. planters covers only windows and beds. railing works on a roof top, not on grass.

need: Options for 1–2 wide openings: a backing or reveal, an infill (framed door or hay opening) so no opening shows a void or see-through slit, and a recess depth for door leaves.
evidence: surround and glazing are tuned for 3+ wide. Builder used grey pane over dark oak backing. Loft door showed a black void. Back slits were see-through. Doors were not recessed.

need: Vertical post rhythm on a wall face (posts every n blocks) that does not grow the grid.
evidence: pilasters every n profile timber grew the grid, so board-and-batten posts were hand-placed on a rhythm.

need: Variant families for single-block materials (terracotta, concrete) or a board-and-batten pattern, so a one-material wall gets rhythm without hand placement.
evidence: Red terracotta has no variant family. vary and weather did nothing on the main wall.

need: When the already-detailed guard skips cells, report the skipped cells, or require an explicit force, rather than skipping roof and surround rules silently.
evidence: Roof and surround rules skipped as already-detailed. force keyword needed to overwrite. Wall recolour reported applied but walls still read white and cream.

need: Per-cell or per-region role declaration so recessed door leaves and deliberate dark accents are not flagged as trim on a red wall.
evidence: Recessed red door leaves flagged as trim until the leaf block changed. Stray dark logs mixed into the red wall.

need: Declared intentional orphans (hanging props, one-block cap tops, interior lights) are accepted, and unsupported finials are flagged.
evidence: check flags hanging bale, pyramid cap top and interior shroomlight as orphans, all intended. A floating spire finial was not caught.

need: A close-up or small-feature view so weather vanes, thin cupolas and 1-wide slits are legible to the judge, not lost at full-building scale.
evidence: Weather vane is a thin line hard to see. Cupola almost invisible from front and side views. Slits visible only in the back view. Evidence that the judge cannot see these is inferred, not measured.

need: Presets for tall conical or pointed caps should default to a height-to-radius ratio that reads as a cone, and warn when the cap is shorter than about 1.5x its eave radius.
evidence: Reviewer Major Roof x2: wide flat-stepped slab with a small spire, cone too short for the brief; fix asked for a cone about twice as tall.

need: Cone roofs should have a fit-inside-footprint option so the eave ring stays within the given grid, instead of extending one block beyond it when grow:false.
evidence: Builder: cone grow ignored grow:false margins; eave ring was R+1 past the footprint, so a 9-wide floor needed a 7-wide footprint argument.

need: Auto-detect should pick the topmost storey's wall top rather than an intermediate beam or jetty course.
evidence: Builder: auto-detect chose the y14 jetty beam course; had to force --y 18.

need: Dormers should work on a leaning or conical roof, sized small (about 3 wide) with a hood, instead of cutting a large hole.
evidence: Builder: dormer on a leaning cone cut a large unreadable hole, so it was turned off and hand-built.

need: Lean should bend smoothly over the upper portion of the cap, not produce a kinked spike at the tip.
evidence: Builder: lean on the cone made a kinked spike at the tip; reviewer said the cone reads as a lid with a spike.

need: Chimneys should work on cone and other non-planar roofs, with the rise measured from the local roof surface and the stack seated in the slope with its own cap.
evidence: Builder: chimneys option unsupported on cone roofs, so the chimney was hand-stacked; reviewer: chimney fused to the spire with a stray flame on top.

tool: roof surface check (mcd check / mcd paint roof)
need: A roof-finish check that flags non-roof-family blocks, stair or glass clutter, and blocks poking out of the slope, plus a palette pass that unifies roof blocks into one family.
evidence: Reviewer Major Finish x2: noisy stair and glass jumble on the roof front, dark-wood stack and orange glass on the slope, stray blocks at the spire base.

need: Roof palettes should support banded courses in a single material family (for example two-tone oxidised copper) so each course reads on a cone.
evidence: Reviewer Major Roof: asked for a two-tone verdigris or single oxidised-copper palette so the courses read as a cone.

need: A jetty brush that builds an overhanging storey from a rectangle with an out distance, a deck, edge beams, and brackets, with a per-storey offset option.
evidence: Builder: jetty deck, edge beams and upside-down stair brackets were hand-looped. Reviewer Minor Massing: jettied floors read as a plain box with a slight overhang.

need: Massing brushes should allow a per-storey lateral shift or lean of a block or two, so a whole tower can read as crooked, not only its roof.
evidence: Reviewer Minor Massing x2: shaft is straight and boxy, so the tower does not look crooked; fix asked for each storey shifted one block sideways.

need: A timber-frame wall brush that lays out plaster infill panels, posts, plates, braces and corner posts for a storey, with a panel-scale variation option.
evidence: Builder: timber-frame wall panel fully hand-looped. Reviewer Minor Facades x2: flat white panels with little relief; asked for timber braces and corner posts.

need: Variation treatments should work at panel scale, so whole infill panels can be darkened or cracked as a unit, not one block at a time.
evidence: Reviewer Minor Facades: plaster panels plain white-grey; rejected Detail task said the changes were too small to read at distance.

need: A window brush for round, oval and octagonal openings with a frame ring and glazing, so circular windows read as circles.
evidence: Builder: no oval or octagon window brush; 3x3 plus of panes by hand. Reviewer Minor Elements x2: round windows read as square panes or slits.

need: A balcony brush that places a deck of a given depth, a connected rail with correct fence states, support brackets, and optional hanging lanterns.
evidence: Builder: balcony deck, connected-fence rail and hanging lanterns hand-placed. Reviewer Minor Elements: balcony tucked away and tiny; asked for a deeper deck and clearer rail.

need: A small prop library for recognisable features such as a telescope, lantern or spyglass, scalable in length and thickness and angled toward a direction.
